You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | U.S.–Iran Fighting Resumes and Oil Rises; Higher September Hike Odds Weigh on Bitcoin and Gold; Nvidia Gives Back Gains After Opening Strong (August 31, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Warsh Reaffirms Inflation Priority; September Hike Pricing Moves Higher
In his Jackson Hole debut, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no explicit rate path, but said that if inflation does not return to 2% “clearly and with sufficient speed,” the Fed would have “more work to do.”
The two-year Treasury yield rose about 11 basis points on the day. CME data show the probability of a 25 bp September hike climbing from about 35% to roughly 58%–60%.
Former Vice Chair Alan Blinder argued the wording itself amounts to another form of forward guidance. Analysts say September payrolls and CPI will still decide the final pricing.
Market Impact : Higher front-end rates pressured richly valued growth stocks and precious metals, while the dollar firmed. If subsequent data weaken again, hike pricing could still fade.
International Commodities
U.S.–Iran Fighting Resumes; Hormuz Risk Premium Returns
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it fired missiles at U.S. bases and accused Washington of bombing facilities on Larak Island, causing casualties. U.S. officials said American forces struck two missile launchers on the island after Iran prepared to fire mine-equipped rockets toward the strait.
U.S. Central Command said it had diverted 83 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the department plans weekly additional secondary sanctions on Iran, starting with banks.
Market Impact : Weekend clashes interrupted hopes of a diplomatic off-ramp. Oil is again pricing supply-disruption risk, lifting both sticky-inflation concerns and safe-haven demand.
Macroeconomic Policy
Trump Says Venezuelan Oil Will Refill the SPR
Trump said the U.S. has reached a deal giving it “majority control” of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s proven reserves and plans to use the oil to refill the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The White House has not released formal agreement details, and markets remain cautious on executability.
Canadian retaliatory tariffs are still due on September 8, so North American trade friction and the energy-supply narrative are running in parallel.
Market Impact : If reserve replenishment materializes, it could ease U.S. pump prices over the medium term. Near-term oil, however, is still driven by Hormuz, leaving a gap between policy signaling and battlefield reality.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,440/oz, -3.4%
Spot Silver : Approx. $66.4/oz, -0.32%
WTI Crude : Approx. $85/bbl, +2.03%
Brent Crude : Approx. $87/bbl, +2.06%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approx. 99.63, -0.04%
Driver Analysis : Warsh’s remarks lifted front-end rates and the dollar. Gold and silver saw clear profit-taking on Friday, with gold falling more than 2% from recent highs. Weekend U.S.–Iran clashes interrupted the “negotiations cooling” trade and put Strait disruption risk back into crude. Institutions see a near-term split: hawkish rates press metals, geopolitics supports oil. Higher oil may reinforce sticky inflation and, in turn, hike pricing—an oil–inflation–rates loop.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $77,625, -0.58%
ETH : Approx. $2,417, -1.62%
Crypto Total Market Cap : Approx. $2.68 trillion, -1%
Market Liquidations : 24-hour liquidations $391 million, of which longs $270 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : BTC around $77,600. Short-liquidation pressure is highly concentrated in the $79,000–$80,000 zone above; a reclaim of $79,000 could trigger a visible short squeeze. Long liquidations are denser near $76,500–$77,500; a break of $77,000 could accelerate leveraged-long liquidations, leaving downside risk intact.
Spot ETF Net Flows : August 28 net outflow about $202 million, ending a nine-session inflow streak.
Driver Analysis : Warsh’s hawkish lean and the ETF swing to outflows interrupted Bitcoin’s momentum after it had reclaimed $80,000. ETH was relatively steadier over the weekend, showing capital did not fully exit risk assets, but crowded high-beta books are still de-levering. Institutional consensus is that rates and geopolitics jointly set the near-term tone. $80,000 has flipped from support to resistance; watch whether funds return ahead of this week’s labor data.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,559.99, -0.02%
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,711.76, -0.25%
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,402.42, -0.52%, as chip stocks gave back the prior session’s gains
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $217.55, -4.57%
AAPL : $319.70, +1.63%
MSFT : $513.53, +1.68%
GOOGL : $346.59, +1.74%
AMZN : $266.43, +3.97%
META : $578.02, +1.21%
TSLA : $348.75, -1.71%
[...]
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : Index losses were modest, but the internal split was sharp. Nvidia’s giveback after Thursday’s surge weighed on the Nasdaq, while Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet attracted flows on Barclays’ thesis that AI inference profits accrue to the cloud majors. Apple was steady; Tesla faded with risk appetite. The market is rotating part of the AI trade from crowded hardware beta toward cloud-infrastructure monetization, reallocating pricing power inside the same theme.
[...]
Representative stocks : Amazon up nearly 4%; Workday up nearly 6%; ServiceNow up more than 4%; Elastic up more than 19%.
[...]
Representative stocks : Nvidia down more than 4%; Intel down nearly 3%; Marvell down about 10%.
[...]
Drivers : Higher hike odds plus some earnings that were “good but not good enough,” plus technical profit-taking after Nvidia’s prior-day surge.
[...]
1. Nvidia (NVDA) – Gives Back More Than 4% the Day After a Surge
[...]
Event Overview : Nvidia fell 4.57% on Friday to $217.55, reversing a sizable share of Thursday’s nearly 9% jump. The company had just reported revenue doubling year-over-year, data-center sales of $89 billion, and about 70% FY2028 growth guidance. The pullback came as Warsh lifted hike odds and Marvell’s results failed to clear a high bar.
[...]
2. Amazon (AMZN) – Cloud-Share Thesis Drives a Nearly 4% Gain
[...]
Event Overview : Amazon rose 3.97% to $266.43, the strongest of the Magnificent Seven. Barclays said that of every $100 in AI-model-company revenue, about $35–$40 is paid as inference compute to AWS, Azure and GCP, of which clouds keep about $10–$20 of operating profit, implying 35%–45% operating margins.
[...]
Market Interpretation : Institutions treat the move as a repricing of AI profit allocation: hardware bottlenecks remain, but incremental profit is increasingly captured in the cloud layer. Analysts caution that margins may fade as compute supply rises and model competition intensifies, so AWS growth and capex efficiency matter more than the snapshot margin.
[...]
3. Microsoft (MSFT) / Alphabet (GOOGL) – Joint Beneficiaries of the Cloud-Inference Narrative
[...]
Event Overview : Microsoft rose 1.68% and Alphabet 1.74%. Barclays grouped Azure and GCP with AWS as core beneficiaries and said lab paid-inference margins have climbed from low double digits in 2025 to 50%–65% in 2026.
[...]
Market Interpretation : Markets are separating “pickaxe sellers” from “cloud sellers.” Microsoft combines models and cloud; Google has in-house TPUs plus a search cash engine. Higher rates still compress multiples, but the fundamental story is more cash-flow oriented than hardware beta.
[...]
Market Interpretation : Institutions say Nvidia has lifted the bar so high that “good growth that is not spectacular” can trigger a valuation reset. Rising hike odds added duration pressure.
[...]
5. Tesla (TSLA) – Energy Narrative Diverges From Risk Appetite
[...]
Event Overview : Tesla fell 1.71% to $348.75. Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla are building 100 GW of annual solar capacity as fast as possible and confirmed SpaceX will cast its own gas-turbine blades to shorten commissioning times.
